title: ACIA Module 1
source_title: CIA Education Syllabus – ACIA Capstone Exam and Modules
intro: The ACIA modules are a core educational requirement toward ACIA designation. They are intended to bridge accredited university education or education obtained via other actuarial organizations with the work environment.
They are administered online via the CIA learning management system.

The modules assume some knowledge of the topics acquired via a recognized university degree or through other Associate-level education. Outcomes that participants are expected to achieve often cover multiple learning objectives, with an emphasis on communications in most tasks.

The modules contain recordings, short readings, and/or quizzes. Each module includes a case study that includes various deliverables such as emails, reports, memorandums, recorded presentations, or spreadsheets. These case studies apply theoretical topics covered in the participant’s university degree or other recognized Associate-level education to practical actuarial scenarios; the content should not be new to the participant, but the application may be.

There is no formal prerequisite for the ACIA modules. Participants in an accredited university will be expected to have completed some actuarial courses prior to completing the first ACIA module, likely in their second year of university.

The second module should be completed when a participant has nearly completed all courses relevant to the ACIA Capstone Exam. It is expected that these participants undertake the second module in the last year of their university program. Participants are responsible for ensuring they have the appropriate knowledge.

topics.title: A. Introduction and actuarial communications
topics.objective: The first portion of the module introduces the profession and gives a general context to the participant; it explains the history of the profession, describes the context of actuarial work and the different fields of practice. Communication in an actuarial setting is also discussed: audiences, technical and non-technical writing, and the impact of cultural diversity on communication. Finally, different channels of oral and written business communication (e.g., email, letter, memorandum, report, summary, presentation deck, messaging, and chat software) are introduced. Their purpose is explained, and the formatting rules for such communication are also exposed.

topics.title: B. The actuarial environment
topics.objective: The second portion of the module describes the actuarial environment: the financial systems, the external forces actuaries are facing, the risks stemming from changes in these external forces. Risk management, quantification, mitigation, and transfer are explained in detail. Emerging risks are also described. Finally, the participant is exposed to the impact of regulations on the environment.

outcomes.text: Understand how business works in various environments.
Outline the context of actuarial work and its main processes.
Define the main steps of risk management: identification, quantification, and mitigation.
Explain the major sources of risk from (changing) external forces and their impact on our financial system.
Describe financial systems within the national and global context.
Describe the main participants in financial markets and explain their objectives and roles.
Describe the major factors affecting the development of financial systems.
Explain the main risks to the stability of national and global financial systems.
Describe the operations, governance structure, legislative framework, capital, and risk management of Canadian financial institutions (e.g., insurance companies, banks).
Describe the determinants of interest rates, price and wage inflation, GDP, and unemployment.
Define external forces.
Categorize the forces (e.g., cultural, demographic, economic, physical) and explain how they fit in the actuarial context.
Explain how changes in external forces can lead to risk.
Define and describe risk management in an actuarial context.
Define risk types and classify them.
Explain how risk can be transferred to others (e.g., hedging, insurance, reinsurance, specialized markets, retained versus ceded).
Explain how to identify new relevant risks.
Describe the impact of climate change and cyber risk on actuarial risks.
Explain blockchain and its impact on risk reduction.
Describe the regulatory context and the impact of regulations on actuarial work.
Describe the international environment for actuarial work.

topics.title: C. Actuarial work
topics.objective: The third portion of the module builds on the actuarial environment and explains how actuaries work to provide sound solutions. An overview of actuarial work is provided, with a particular emphasis on the distinction between actuarial work and that of other financial experts. The actuarial control cycle is introduced, and each component of actuarial work is described. Decision-making and problem solving, and ethics and professionalism are also introduced.
